summary.headline: KISCO Holdings to take Hankook Steel wholly owned via share exchange; buyback price raised to KRW 13,000
summary.what_happened: On Nov 27, 2026, KISCO Holdings Corp. corrected its Oct 30, 2026 material-event report on a share exchange with Hankook Steel (한국철강), under which KISCO Holdings is to become Hankook Steel's wholly owning parent. Following a tender offer at KRW 13,000 per share, KISCO Holdings' stake in Hankook Steel was revised to 78.34% of issued shares, and Hankook Steel's board raised the share-purchase-claim price for dissenting shareholders from KRW 9,700 to KRW 13,000 per share.

key_numbers.label: KISCO Holdings' stake in Hankook Steel after tender offer

summary.why_it_matters: In Korea, share exchanges that make a company a wholly owned subsidiary typically require the subsidiary's minority shareholders to exchange their shares for the parent's shares, and shareholders who object may exercise share-purchase claims at a price set under law or agreed with the company. Such filings generally indicate the terms and pricing that minority holders may receive, which depend on the outcome of shareholder meetings and any later agreement on price.
